title: Truthful speech
tomorrow: kiran calls. simran has advice ready. why does it go wrong?

segments.voice: Yesterday, no slander: don't call anyone bad, especially to an audience. The joke stayed unsent. Somebody noticed.

11:48 p.m. A text from Kiran, who hasn't messaged Simran since sophomore biology: is everyone talking about me? Simran stares at it. Yes is true, and it would land like a slap. No would be easier, and it would be a lie. Somewhere between them there's a third answer, and she can't find it. The help she reaches for is a strange line, one that seems to put something above truth itself.
screen: `11:48 P.M. A TEXT FROM KIRAN.` → `YES WOULD SLAP. NO WOULD LIE.` → `A THIRD ANSWER?`

segments.voice: On Ang 62, in Sri Raag, Guru Nanak says: truth is higher than everything. Then, in the same breath: higher still is truthful living. Wait. What could be above truth? Here's how the puzzle comes apart. In Gurbani, sach, truth, isn't only a fact you get right. The Japji opens by calling the One true in the beginning, true through the ages. Truth is a name for the Real itself. So truthful living is a life lined up with that: true in what you say, and true in how and why you say it. A fact thrown like a rock can be accurate and still miss. Yesterday's line said don't call anyone bad. Today's adds the other half: don't call anything fine that isn't. No lie to spare someone. No wound to prove you're honest. Here's the line worth repeating tonight: in Gurbani, the truth is meant to be lived, not thrown. So Simran writes, deletes, writes again. Some people were. It wasn't fair, and I don't think it's true. Are you okay? She reads it twice. It's true. It's kind. She sends it at 11:56, and the three dots appear right away.
screen: `ANG 62: TRUTH IS HIGHER THAN ALL.` · `HIGHER STILL: TRUTHFUL LIVING.` · `SACH: A NAME FOR THE REAL.` · `NO LIE TO SPARE, NO WOUND TO PROVE.` · then, large: `TRUE AND KIND.`

segments.voice: If there's paper near you, write one true thing you've been holding back from someone. Read it once as it is. Then rewrite it so it stays completely true and lands more kindly, and leave the page beside you for the sit.
Truthful speech. Words that are accurate, from a life lined up with the truth. Sach is truth.
True and kind: the line asks for both at once, in the same breath. That's day sixteen ninety-six.

screen: `DAY 1696 COUNTS.` → `LIVING IT · 70 OF 134.` → `TOMORROW: KIRAN CALLS. WHY DOES THE ADVICE GO WRONG?`

howItsDone: Guru Nanak's line on Ang 62, that truthful living is higher even than truth, is why Sikh teaching counts how and why something is said as part of honesty.

fork.setup: a friend asks if her college essay is good. honestly, it's not there yet, and it's due friday. what's truthful speech here?
options: say it's not there yet, and name the part that really works.
say it's great; she's stressed and it's too late to fix it.
list every problem; real honesty means holding nothing back.
fork.reveal: truthful living sits above bare truth: no lie to spare her, no wound to prove you're honest. true, and kind, and still useful by friday.
